subject: general
question: What was the effect of controlled seasonal grazing by sheep in the alpine meadows of the Himalayan National Park?

options.text: It destroyed the ground cover and led to soil erosion.
It had no effect because sheep were few and the Park is vast.
It removed older grass and allowed new grass to grow.
The National Park provided income and livelihood to the local shepherds.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It removed older grass and allowed new grass to grow.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Controlled seasonal grazing by sheep in the alpine meadows of the Himalayan National Park had ecological benefits,** such as removing older grass, which made space for new and fresh grass to grow.
 
• This practice, when managed well, **can help maintain the balance of the ecosystem.**
 
• Grazing removes older, senescent grass**, making space for new, nutrient-rich growth**.
 
• This** enhances the productivity of the meadow.**
 
• Grazing can maintain habitat heterogeneity, supporting various plant and animal species that depend on open or patchy vegetation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP):

 
• The Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP), which is one of India's national parks, is located in the Kullu region in the state of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• Great Himalayan National Park, oldest and largest National park in the state.
 
• The park was established in 1984 and is spread over an area of 1171 km2 at an altitude of between 1500 and 6000 m.
 
• The Great Himalayan National Park is a habitat to numerous flora and more than 375 fauna species, including approximately 31 mammals, 181 birds, 3 reptiles, 9 amphibians, 11 annelids, 17 molluscs and 127 insects.
 
• They are protected under the strict guidelines of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 hence any sort of hunting is not permitted.
 
• In June 2014, the Great Himalayan National Park was added to the UNESCO list of World Heritage Sites. 
 
• The UNESCO World Heritage Site Committee granted the status to the park under the criteria of "outstanding significance for biodiversity conservation.
